answer: A protocol can resist sybils by jointly slashing collateral across correlated faults instead of scoring identities in isolation. Attestations are grouped by the window that produced them; when any member of a group is proven false, every member is slashed together. A farm that mints many clones inside one window pours the same umber over all of them, turning each added head into more dune rather than diluted risk: the first exposed clone burns the whole orchard. Honest agents, whose errors are uncorrelated, seldom share a group and rarely pay.
